name: Phonely
positioning: A voice-agent platform with a visual flow builder, A/B testing and analytics, aimed at everyone from small businesses to large contact centres.

pricing.model: Monthly subscription with included minutes plus overage; Enterprise is quoted per minute.
pricing.headline: Free (100 min), Starter $50/mo, Pro $150/mo billed monthly (or $33 and $100/mo billed annually); Enterprise from about 5 cents/min.
planNotes: Starter: $50/mo monthly or $33/mo annual; the page shows both 200 and 250 included minutes in different places.
Pro: $150/mo monthly or $100/mo annual; the page shows both 650 and 750 included minutes in different places.
Enterprise: 'as low as 5 cents/min', billed monthly, quote via sales (includes full agent build-out, SIP trunking, HIPAA BAA per the plan card).
Overage listed as $0.25-$0.35/min on Starter (the page shows both values), $0.30/min on Pro, $0.25/min on Enterprise.
Post-transfer rate listed as $0.02/min on paid plans.
pricing.freeTrial: Free plan with 100 minutes (no card requirement stated on the pages read).
whatIsExtra: Overage minutes beyond the plan allowance.
Post-transfer minutes at a listed per-minute rate.

strengths.claim: Offers a free plan with 100 minutes and a self-serve AI builder, so a team can test before paying.
Docs describe a flow editor, A/B testing, unit testing, call history and analytics (call paths, topics, sentiment) inside the product.
Publishes an API covering agent generation from a prompt, duplicate agent, call listing, knowledge-base documents and Twilio number import.
States SOC 2, GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA and PCI compliance on its homepage, with a HIPAA BAA on Enterprise.
Supports outbound campaigns as well as inbound agents, with documented outbound compliance guidance.

limitations.claim: Phonely's pricing page shows different included-minute and overage figures in different places (200 vs 250, 650 vs 750; $0.25 vs $0.35), so plan allowances should be confirmed with the vendor.
Twilio is the number-import source accepted by the documented Import Number API, and the agent must be on a paid plan.

integrations: CRM integrations (named on the pricing page, providers not listed there)

compliance.note: Stated by vendor, self-attested: homepage lists SOC 2, GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA and PCI; pricing page lists 'SOC2 & GDPR' and a HIPAA BAA signature (shown with the Enterprise plan). Which plans include each item is shown with icons that could not be read as text.

telephony.providedNumbers: Plans include provided numbers (1 on Free, 3 on Starter, 5 on Pro). Twilio numbers can be imported via API on paid plans; SIP trunking is listed with the Enterprise plan.

stepsToLeave: Agents: the Get Agent / Get Agents API returns 'basic information'; no documented full export of flows was found, so flows would be recreated by hand in the new platform.
Knowledge base: List Documents and List Websites API endpoints exist to enumerate sources so they can be re-added elsewhere.
Call data: List Calls / Get Call API and CSV usage export (Settings > Usage & Cost) are documented.
Numbers: a number imported from a Twilio account stays in that account; for numbers provided by Phonely, no porting procedure was found in the docs read.

bestFor: Teams that want a flow-based builder with built-in testing and analytics, from a free trial up to large enterprise volumes.
unknowns: Exact included minutes (200 vs 250 Starter; 650 vs 750 Pro) and Starter overage ($0.25 vs $0.35) conflict on the pricing page.
Which compliance items apply to which plan (shown as icons).
Whether full agent/flow export or number porting out is supported.
Per-minute cost of the LLM, voice and telephony on self-serve plans (not itemised on pages read).
